$what: Provenance of aurora-effects-preset.schema.json — empyrean's CONTRACT schema for the wave-2 RASTER PRESET document (bands), vendored into Aurora beside the codec that validates against it. preset.ts imports the .json directly; this sidecar records where those bytes came from, and test/formats/effects-preset-schema-drift.test.ts reads `empyrean.blob` from here as its pin of record.
$why_a_sidecar_and_not_a_test_constant: The scene schema's pin lived as a const in one test AND as prose in two other files, and the prose copies went three re-pins stale without anything going red, because nothing hashes a comment. That lesson was applied when the scene pin moved here on 2026-08-29; this file is born with it. The hash lives HERE, once, and the test reads it.
$why_vendored: Aurora's core must validate from a lone clone, inside a git worktree (where ../../empyrean is not where it is from master), and in a packaged Electron build that ships no sibling repo. A path-probe design would degrade to 'schema not found -> skip validation', which is the loud-on-unmeasurable failure this suite is not allowed to have. The cost of vendoring is staleness; the drift gate is the payment.
$this_document_is_not_a_scene: A BAND IS NOT A SCENE FIELD. A scene is a parallax_config; the raster program is a channel of an EffectsPreset, bound per SECTION. A `bands` key on a scene file is refused by the scene loader's closed-schema path, deliberately. These are two schemas and two directories, and conflating them is the failure this whole sidecar pair exists to make impossible.

aurora_edits_this_vendoring_forced.json_schema_subset: This schema is the first committed contract schema to put `unevaluatedProperties: false` beside an in-place applicator — at $defs.band.properties.on, where `oneOf: [{required:[cram]},{required:[pal_region]}]` spells the exactly-one-arm rule. json-schema-subset.ts refused that combination outright. The refusal was a FALSE POSITIVE here (a `required`-only branch contributes no property annotations, so the additionalProperties equivalence holds exactly), and it was narrowed to a PROVER, `contributesPropertyAnnotations`, that clears a branch only when every keyword in it is on a whitelist of provably-inert ones. $ref/$dynamicRef stay an unconditional refusal because their value is a string this evaluator does not follow.
aurora_edits_this_vendoring_forced.why_a_whitelist: The failure this evaluator exists to prevent is silently ACCEPTING what the real schema rejects. A blacklist is wrong by default on every keyword nobody thought of; a whitelist is right by default and merely inconvenient when the schema grows.
aurora_edits_this_vendoring_forced.type_arrays_12aecd5: The 12aecd5 amendment spelled `cycles` as `"type": ["array", "null"]` — the first type ARRAY in a committed contract schema. json-schema-subset.ts refused type arrays inside validateNode, i.e. only on a node a DOCUMENT reached; `type` was already an implemented keyword NAME, so the keyword-coverage gate stayed GREEN while the first document carrying `cycles` threw UnsupportedSchemaError. Two edits: (1) `type` now accepts a list of implemented type names, meaning any-of, refused by name in assertSupported before any value is seen; (2) a whole-schema walker, `assertSchemaSupported`, runs the per-node check over every node reachable or not, and both drift gates call it — because a keyword NAME can be implemented while a VALUE SHAPE of it is not, and only a walk sees the shape.
aurora_edits_this_vendoring_forced.nothing_forced_at_d36d704: The patch_world_ys / patch_motion amendment forced NO edit to json-schema-subset.ts, and that is a MEASURED result, not an assumption: the keyword census, the whole-schema walk (assertSchemaSupported) and the vectors were all run against the newly vendored bytes before this line was written. Every construct the amendment uses was already implemented and already exercised — `$ref` inside a `oneOf` branch (variants' null-slot shape), a bare `not: {const: N}` (the scene schema's drift.rate hole), `minimum`/`maximum`, `maxItems`, and `unevaluatedProperties: false` beside plain `properties`/`required` (patch_motion_entry, anchor_sweep). The one shape worth naming because it looks like the 6664b61 false positive and is NOT one: `$defs.patch_motion_entry` carries `unevaluatedProperties: false` with NO in-place applicator beside it, so the additionalProperties equivalence holds without needing the `contributesPropertyAnnotations` prover at all.
aurora_edits_this_vendoring_forced.root_oneOf_9233883:
THE 9233883 AMENDMENT PUT AN `oneOf` AT THE DOCUMENT ROOT, beside `properties`, `required` and `unevaluatedProperties: false` — the same in-place-applicator shape $defs.band.properties.on already carried, hoisted to cover the whole document. TWO SEPARATE ANSWERS, both MEASURED against the newly vendored bytes rather than carried over from d36d704's 'nothing forced' (a different amendment, and that finding does not transfer):
  (1) validateAgainstSchema NEEDED NO EDIT. Measured four ways on the real schema: `bands` only ACCEPTS, `ramp` only ACCEPTS, BOTH is refused ('matches 2 of the 2 allowed forms'), NEITHER is refused ('matches none of the 2'). The keyword census is clean and assertSchemaSupported walks the whole file without throwing. The rows live in test/formats/effects-preset-ramp.test.ts.
  (2) canonicalizeBySchema DID need an edit, and this is the finding the four-way probe turned up beside it. Its `oneOf` arm recursed into the winning branch and RETURNED, DISCARDING the sibling `properties` — and the winning branch here is `{required: ['bands']}`, which declares no properties, so the function fell straight through to `return value` and SILENTLY SKIPPED the undeclared-key refusal that is the only thing it still exists for. Measured: a document with a `bogus_key` at the root came back with the key intact. The same hole was ALREADY OPEN at $defs.band.properties.on (an `on` object carrying an undeclared key survived canonicalization too) — pre-existing since 6664b61, invisible because validation refuses that document first, and hoisting the shape to the root is what made it worth finding. Fixed by asking `contributesPropertyAnnotations` — the prover assertSupported already uses for exactly this question — whether the winning branch can contribute property annotations: when it provably cannot (a `required`-only arm rule), canonicalization continues with THIS node's own keywords minus the `oneOf`, instead of replacing them.
aurora_edits_this_vendoring_forced.multipleOf_5bd76ba: THE 5bd76ba AMENDMENT FORCED ONE EDIT, AND IT WAS A LOUD FAILURE RATHER THAN A SILENT ONE. `$defs.base_swap.properties.target` carries `multipleOf: 8192` — THE FIRST `multipleOf` IN ANY COMMITTED CONTRACT SCHEMA. json-schema-subset.ts did not implement the keyword, so it threw UnsupportedSchemaError ('refusing to validate rather than ignoring it') on EVERY base_swap document, which is the designed behaviour and is why the failure was visible instead of the keyword quietly becoming a no-op. Implemented as a division test (`Number.isInteger(value / multipleOf)`), the spec's own spelling rather than `%`, and added to ASSERTION_KEYWORDS and to NON_ANNOTATING_KEYWORDS (it is a pure numeric assertion and can name no property as evaluated, so the `unevaluatedProperties` equivalence is unaffected). THE THIRD ROOT `oneOf` ARM FORCED NOTHING, AND THAT IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: the nine-case matrix in test/formats/effects-preset-base-swap.test.ts runs each arm alone (ACCEPT), every pair and the triple (REFUSE), none (REFUSE), and — the case that broke silently at 9233883 — a bogus root key beside a valid arm ONCE PER ARM (REFUSE). The `contributesPropertyAnnotations` fix from 9233883 does hold on the third arm; the rows prove it rather than inheriting it.
aurora_edits_this_vendoring_forced.nothing_forced_at_e9409dc_but_the_codec_: THE EVALUATOR WAS UNTOUCHED AND THE CODEC WAS NOT, and the distinction is the whole lesson of this landing. json-schema-subset.ts needed no edit — measured, not assumed: the schema is structurally identical (see the pin history's stripped-comparison), so no keyword, type array or value shape is new. But `preset.ts` READS PROSE, and prose is exactly what moved. Any future 'description-only' CR must be checked against every schemaNumberFromProse() derivation in preset.ts before it is called a no-op; there are several, and each one turns a sentence into a number that reaches a renderer. ⚠ AND THE TWO RAMP DISPLAY SENTENCES LIVE IN DIFFERENT NODES: the span bound and the per-field rules are on $defs.ramp, the per-index and CRAM sentences on the KEY paragraph properties.ramp. My first derivation read the wrong node and threw at module load with the regex printed — the loud parse doing its job on its first real outing.

cram_is_stated_but_cannot_be_authored: e9409dc's ramp paragraph states a CRAM display rule — value j displays on top + j, ONE LINE EARLIER than VSRAM, because the N+1 latency is VSRAM's alone. THERE IS NO CRAM ARM: $defs.ramp_target has properties {vsram}, required [vsram] and unevaluatedProperties false, so no document can carry one and Aurora ships no CRAM path. Recorded here, in preset.ts's docblock, AND pinned by the derived EFFECTS_PRESET_RAMP_TARGET_ARMS, whose module-load guard throws naming the one-line difference if an arm is ever added — because a comment is what goes stale and a guard is what does not.
